items.title: Chuck Israels interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 11, 2021
items.q: I go up to Milt and say, “ Gee Milt, please turn that off.

ctx.x: Isn’t it interesting to be sitting in a restaurant like that and thinking am I the only one in here who is driven to distraction by this music?

Yeah. I also have had the experience of being at a party where I was specifically invited, graciously, as a new faculty member by another faculty member wanting to introduce me to his friends and make me feel welcome. And I’m at this party at this nice guy’s house and he’s playing a Monk record. And we’re standing around having a conversation and I go up to Milt and say, “ Gee Milt, please turn that off. I can’t talk to people, I have to listen to that. It’s not background to me.”
Interesting. And there was a time when you didn’t like Thelonious Monk, isn’t that true?
